why: The documented P2/P3 boundary (roadmap §3.2 row 7): `my $log = Shop::Log->new; $log->write` and `$thing->write` on a parameter are both receiver-typed calls P2 deliberately does not resolve — only P3's typed-receiver rule does, and only for the literal-constructor shape (`$log`), never a bare parameter (`$thing` has no declared type to resolve, a permanent miss even after P3). `Shop::Log->new` itself (a qualified-receiver call, §3.2 row 3) is unrelated to this boundary and resolves in P2 like any other qualified call — this case's job is to prove P2 does NOT also resolve the two instance calls just because the qualified one nearby does.

known_gaps.why: PREDICTED BEFORE SCORING. `$log` holds a literal `Shop::Log->new` constructor in the same sub — P3's typed-receiver rule resolves this; P2 does not.
PREDICTED BEFORE SCORING. `$thing` is an untyped parameter with no declared type to resolve from — a permanent miss, not just a P2-vs-P3 gap.
